definitions.explanation: A person, especially a young woman, who dances professionally or as a performer. Often evokes a traditional or literary image.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}の{踊|おど}り{子|こ}が{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The dancer on stage was beautiful.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りで{踊|おど}り{子|こ}たちが{華|はな}やかに{踊|おど}った。
examples.english: The dancers performed brilliantly at the festival.

examples.japanese: {川端康成|かわばたやすなり}の『{伊豆|いず}の{踊|おど}り{子|こ}』は{日本文学|にほんぶんがく}の{名作|めいさく}として{広|ひろ}く{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Kawabata Yasunari's 'The Izu Dancer' is widely known as a masterpiece of Japanese literature.

notes:
Compound of {踊|おど}り (dancing) + {子|こ} (person, child). The word carries a traditional, somewhat romantic connotation compared to the modern loanword ダンサー.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭|まつ}りの{踊|おど}り{子|こ} (festival dancer)
- {踊|おど}り{子|こ}たちが{舞|ま}う (dancers perform)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{川端康成|かわばたやすなり}の{短編|たんぺん}{小説|しょうせつ}『{伊豆|いず}の{踊|おど}り{子|こ}』(The Izu Dancer, 1926) is one of the most famous works in Japanese literature, telling the story of a student's encounter with a troupe of traveling performers. The word {踊|おど}り{子|こ} is strongly associated with this work.
